findings.failure_consequence: one corrupt byte (strict UTF-8 decode) or one kirby exception on any line kills the loop; restart replays from offset 0 and crashes again identically - persistent crash loop needing manual surgery (truncate the signal file).
findings.fix: owner isolates poison lines (errors='replace' or per-line try/except with skip-ahead offset + dead-letter note) so one bad line cannot pin the loop
findings.smallest_targeted_test: signal file with one invalid-UTF-8 byte mid-stream -> assert loop processes surrounding lines and continues (crashes today, and again after restart)

findings.failure_consequence: concurrent lane appends can interleave mid-line (buffered IO splits the single logical write), producing garbage lines that are consumed as events and never reassembled. Same class as F-CONT-1.
findings.fix: owner serializes appends (lock file) or documents single-writer + atomic-rename discipline
findings.smallest_targeted_test: two processes append 1000 lines concurrently -> assert all lines intact (interleaving possible today)

findings.failure_consequence: a reader catching a torn tail feeds a garbage line once (usually IGNORED/STILL_OPEN fail-closed; an OUTPUT fragment could falsely trip the saturation scan) and the remainder is never reassembled.
findings.fix: owner only consumes \n-terminated lines, holding the offset at the last newline
findings.smallest_targeted_test: signal file ending mid-line -> assert offset stays at last newline and no partial line is fed (consumed today)

findings.failure_consequence: minor crashes/spins on edge inputs instead of steady looping.
findings.fix: owner uses state.get('offset',0), guards the notice append, and clamps interval to a positive floor
findings.title: small robustness warts: run_once({}) KeyError on state['offset'] (line 72 strict vs line 70 tolerant); unwritable NOTICES dir raises out of run_once and kills the loop; --interval 0/negative busy-spins

findings.failure_consequence: every restart re-emits a notice for a still-pending wake; consumers must dedupe by the (session_id, workkey, token) triple carried in the record.
findings.fix: owner persists notified triples (or documents per-lifetime semantics + downstream-dedupe contract) and fsyncs the notice log
findings.title: notice dedup is process-local (in-memory triple) + NOTICES log not fsynced: 'at most ONE wake notice per pending continuation' holds per process lifetime only
